  • Reference

    Taxonomic classification of prey identified in common sole

    species_classif.Rd

    Reference table providing the taxonomic classification of organisms identified in the digestive tract contents of common sole (Solea solea) during the CAPES project.

    Format

    A tibble with 29 variables:

    scientific_name

    Character. Scientific name or taxonomic identifier recorded in the stomach content dataset. Names may correspond to species, genera, families, or higher taxonomic groups.

    Kingdom

    Character. Taxonomic kingdom.

    Subkingdom

    Character. Taxonomic subkingdom.

    Infrakingdom

    Character. Taxonomic infrakingdom.

    Phylum

    Character. Taxonomic phylum.

    Subphylum

    Character. Taxonomic subphylum.

    Infraphylum, Parvphylum

    Character. Additional taxonomic subdivisions of the phylum.

    Gigaclass, Superclass, Class, Subclass, Infraclass, Subterclass

    Character. Taxonomic class and its subdivisions or higher classification levels.

    Superorder, Order, Suborder, Infraorder, Parvorder

    Character. Taxonomic order and its subdivisions or higher classification levels.

    Section, Subsection

    Character. Additional intermediate taxonomic ranks.

    Superfamily, Family, Subfamily, Tribe

    Character. Taxonomic family and its subdivisions or higher classification levels.

    Genus

    Character. Taxonomic genus.

    Subgenus

    Character. Taxonomic subgenus, when applicable.

    Species

    Character. Scientific name at the species level, when the organism was identified to species.

    Subspecies

    Character. Scientific name at the subspecies level, when applicable.

    Source

    CAPES project stomach content dataset. Taxonomic classification retrieved from the World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS).

    Details

    Taxonomic information was retrieved from the World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS). The dataset contains the scientific name recorded in the stomach content data and its corresponding taxonomic hierarchy, from kingdom to species or the lowest available taxonomic rank.

    Each row represents a taxon recorded in the stomach content dataset. Taxonomic classification was obtained using the R package worrms, which provides access to the World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS).

    Taxa identified only to genus or a higher taxonomic rank retain their available classification without being assigned to an arbitrary species. For example, a record identified as "Spisula sp" may have a classification extending to the genus "Spisula", while its Species field remains missing.

    Missing values indicate that the corresponding taxonomic rank was not available or was not applicable to the taxon. Some ranks are specific to particular taxonomic groups and are therefore not populated for all organisms.

    The scientific_name variable can be used to join this reference table to the stomach content dataset.

    See also

    soles_stomach, benthos_info
